title: Procurement, Contract Lifecycle, and Revenue Controls Playbook
author: Marisol Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook defines the end-to-end controls and operational steps for budgeting & forecasting, procurement & vendor commitments, contract lifecycle management (CLM), and revenue recognition / billing policies at Redwood Inference. The goal is to balance speed for product teams with finance and legal guardrails that ensure accurate financial reporting, vendor risk mitigation, and consistent customer billing.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood business units and product teams that: enter vendor contracts, commit capital or operational spend, sign customer agreements, or request invoicing/credits.
- Exclusions: compensation and payroll (people-ops) and investor transactions (finance-legal escalations required).

Ownership and Roles

- Finance: overall owner for budgeting, forecasting, revrec policy, and invoicing accuracy. (Primary contact: Marisol Chen).
- Legal: contract review, negotiation guardrails, signature authority matrix, and redline policy.
- Procurement: vendor onboarding, PO issuance, and supplier risk checks.
- Requesting team (Engineering/Product/Sales): provides business justification, budget code, and acceptance criteria for deliverables.

Key Principles

1. Separation of duties: approvals, contract negotiation, and invoice processing must be performed by distinct roles.
2. Principle-based thresholds: higher-risk commitments require additional review (see approval matrix).
3. Revenue recognition will follow ASC 606-aligned principles: identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price, and recognize when obligations are satisfied.
4. Maintain an auditable trail: all contract files, POs, and invoices must be stored in the finance document repository with versioning.

Budgeting & Forecasting (process summary)

- Cadence: Annual budgeting (Nov–Dec) with quarterly reforecasts and monthly close variance analysis.
- Inputs: pipeline (sales), committed spend (contracts/POs), headcount plans, model serving capacity (Dedicated/Private capacity commitments), and historical unit economics (cost per 1k tokens).
- Outputs: P&L by product line, cash-flow runway, and capital commitment tracker.

Quarterly forecast steps (owner: Finance Business Partner):
1. Circulate forecast template to owners (product, eng, sales).
2. Owners upload line-level assumptions and explain major variances.
3. Finance consolidates and runs sensitivity scenarios (best / base / downside).
4. FP&A reviews with execs; approved forecast is published to the leadership portal.

Procurement Procedures

A. Vendor Selection and Risk Assessment
- For purchases > $50k (annualized) a vendor risk assessment (security, financial, data residency) is required. Procurement coordinates assessment with Security and Legal.
- Preferred vendors: those in the approved vendor registry with reference checks and insurance certificates on file.

B. Purchase Order (PO) and Commitment Process
- All commitments must be recorded with a PO or contract. Ad-hoc spend without a PO older than 30 days will trigger a compliance review.
- PO generation flow: Requestor -> Procurement -> Finance approves budget code -> PO issued -> Vendor receives PO -> Goods/Services received -> Invoice matched and paid.

Approval Matrix (illustrative)

| Commitment type | Threshold | Approver(s) | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Operational subscriptions (SaaS) | <= $10k | Team lead | Auto-approve via procurement portal |
| Operational subscriptions | $10k–$50k | Manager + Procurement | Procurement negotiates terms |
| Capital / Dedicated infra commitments | $50k–$250k | Director Finance + Legal | Contract review required |
| Strategic / Multi-year commitments | > $250k | CFO + General Counsel | Exec sign-off & board notification if > $1M |

C. Emergency procurements
- If an emergency procurement is required (security incident, critical outage), the on-call procurement lead may approve up to $100k but must document justification and obtain retroactive sign-off from Finance within 48 hours.

Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)

Stages and minimum controls:
1. Request & Intake: Requestor files a CLM intake form with SOW, budget code, and escalation contacts.
2. Business Terms: Product/Revenue owners define commercial terms (price, billing cadence, SLAs, termination rights).
3. Legal Review: Legal performs contract risk scoring (IP, indemnities, data processing terms).
4. Negotiation: Use standard redline playbook; deviations > 3 clauses escalate to GC.
5. Signature & Archival: Only authorized signatories may execute. Signed contracts are uploaded to the CLM system with tags (customer/vendor, term, auto-renew).
6. Post-signature Obligations: Finance records deferred revenue / prepaid expenses, Procurement tracks vendor delivery, Product verifies acceptance criteria.

Signature Authority (summary)
- Manager-level: up to $50k for pre-approved templates.
- Director-level: up to $250k with Legal approval.
- CFO/GC: > $250k or any contract with atypical indemnities/data transfer clauses.

Legal redline guardrails (common no-go terms unless escalated)
- Unlimited liability for breaches tied to our negligence.
- Broad customer audit rights without scope/time limits.
- Cross-jurisdiction data transfers without DPA consent.
- Auto-renew clauses without explicit notification windows unless aligned with product pricing policy.

Revenue Recognition and Billing Policies

Principles (ASC 606-aligned)
1. Identify the contract with a customer: signed agreement that creates enforceable rights.
2. Identify performance obligations: discrete deliverables (API access, compute hours, embeddings delivery).
3. Determine transaction price: include discounts, usage estimates, and variable consideration with constraint.
4. Allocate price to performance obligations: based on standalone selling price or best estimate.
5. Recognize revenue when (or as) performance obligations are satisfied.

Common Redwood scenarios and treatment
- Hosted API (usage-based monthly billing): revenue recognized as tokens are delivered (ratably) over the billing month. Deferred revenue recorded at invoice if prepayment exists.

- Dedicated capacity (reserved monthly/annual commitment + overage): base reservation recognized ratably over the reservation term. Overage recognized when earned (usage-based) and invoiced in the following month.

- Private deployments (license + services + support): separate software license (if perpetual) recognized per license guidance; implementation services recognized over time as services are delivered using input method; support recognized ratably over support term.

- Multi-element arrangements: allocate transaction price to each distinct obligation. Example: deployment + training + 12 months support -> allocate based on SSP and recognize as each obligation is satisfied.

Billing cadence and invoicing
- Standard: Monthly invoices for usage and subscription. Net30 unless negotiated otherwise.
- Annual prepaid contracts: invoice at contract inception; revenue recognized ratably over the contract period unless deliverables cause different timing.
- Credits & refunds: Sales credits must be approved by Finance and logged with a credit memo. Refunds > $5k require VP Finance approval.

Deferred revenue and journal entries (examples)
- Annual prepaid subscription ($120,000 for 12 months) at inception:
```
Dr Cash 120,000
  Cr Deferred Revenue 120,000
Monthly recognition (1/12):
Dr Deferred Revenue 10,000
  Cr Revenue 10,000
```
- Usage invoice recognized on issuance (no prepayment):
```
Dr Accounts Receivable 5,000
  Cr Revenue 5,000
```

Collections and Credit Control

- Collections owner: Billing team (Finance ops).
- Late payment policy: invoices 30 days past due escalate to Sales/Account owner; 60+ days overdue triggers credit hold; 90+ days overdue escalates to Legal for collections.

Audit and Controls for RevRec

- Monthly close checklist: recon of deferred revenue, contract population check (CLM vs GL), journal entry substantiation.
- Quarterly audit-prep: provide a samples register, contract copies, and evidence of performance obligations.
- Materiality thresholds for audit sampling: > $50k per contract or 5% of segment revenue (whichever is lower).

Operational Tools and Templates

- Approved documents: PO template, CLM intake form, standard customer master data checklist, DPA template, subscription order form. (See attachments in CLM system.)
- Systems: ERP = NetLedger (finance), CLM = ContractHub, Procurement portal = ProcureX. Integrations: ContractHub -> NetLedger syncs signed contract terms to deferred revenue schedules.

Exception Handling and Escalation Paths

- If revenue recognition treatment is in doubt (e.g., variable consideration or significant financing component), escalate to Controller and Legal for a documented policy decision.
- Procurement disputes (non-delivery, SLA breach) escalate to Procurement lead and Legal within 5 business days of identifying the issue.

Appendix A: Example Approval Email Template

Subject: Approval Request – Vendor OR Customer Contract (Vendor/Customer name)
Body:
- Requestor: [name, team]
- Contract value: $[amount]
- Budget Code: [GL code]
- Term: [start] to [end]
- Business rationale: [short bullets]
- Requested approvers: [list]

Appendix B: Change Log

- 2024-09-15: Initial draft.
- 2024-11-02: Updated procurement thresholds after quarterly ops review.
- 2025-02-10: Revised emergency procurement limits and added NetLedger/ContractHub integration notes.

Contact and escalation

For questions about this playbook, contact Finance (finance@redwood.ai) or Legal (legal@redwood.ai). For urgent revrec questions during close, page the Controller on-call.
